requirements.title: A CLOSE statement is CLOSE with a parenthesized close-spec list
requirements.definition: The CLOSE statement syntax is the keyword CLOSE followed by parentheses containing a close-spec-list.

pending.close-keyword-parentheses: Positive-control source uses CLOSE (10) after opening unit 10; syntax-only negatives repair missing parentheses or misspelled keyword without changing the unit setup.
pending.close-spec-list-required: Diagnostic/control source uses CLOSE () and repairs only by adding an existing opened unit number; the repaired program closes a pre-opened file so the spec list is load-bearing.

requirements.oracle: Plans are pending and source-derived. Positive plans establish a non-default state first (for example by opening a known file, writing known records, initializing variables to nonzero/nonblank sentinels, or using a distinct labelled control path) and then observe only portable properties: successful IOSTAT zero, nonzero IOSTAT for a specified error condition, exact internal records or file existence where the source fixes it, or named intrinsic status values where the standard names them. Processor-dependent unit numbers, file names, storage encodings, buffering, timing, IOMSG text, and specific numeric status values are not asserted.

requirements.title: A close-spec is UNIT, IOSTAT, IOMSG, ERR, or STATUS
requirements.definition: A close-spec is one of file-unit-number with optional UNIT=, IOSTAT= stat-variable, IOMSG= iomsg-variable, ERR= label, or STATUS= scalar-default-character-expression.

pending.close-spec-unit: Positive-control source opens a known unit and closes it with CLOSE(UNIT=unit); a positional form is credited through C1208.
pending.close-spec-iostat: Initialize an integer stat variable to a sentinel, close a controlled open unit with IOSTAT=stat, and assert only zero/nonzero as fixed by 12.11 after that section is registered.
pending.close-spec-iomsg: Use an IOMSG character variable initialized to nonblank sentinels only to establish syntax admission; no comparison of message text is a portable oracle.
pending.close-spec-err: Use ERR=label with an in-scope branch target and a controlled error case only after 12.11 establishes the branch condition; the label path sets a nondefault marker.
pending.close-spec-status: Close a named existing file with STATUS="KEEP" and then reopen/read known content; a DELETE counterpart uses a separate file and observes absence only through portable existence inquiry.

requirements.title: No close-spec appears more than once in a CLOSE specifier list
requirements.definition: No specifier shall appear more than once in a given close-spec-list.

requirements.title: A CLOSE specifier list specifies a file-unit-number and positional UNIT comes first
requirements.definition: A file-unit-number shall be specified in a close-spec-list; if UNIT= is omitted, the file-unit-number shall be the first item in the list.

pending.close-file-unit-required: Diagnostic/control source uses CLOSE(IOSTAT=stat) with no file-unit-number, repairing only by adding UNIT=opened_unit; the repaired source closes a known open file.
pending.positional-close-unit-first: Diagnostic/control source uses CLOSE(IOSTAT=stat, opened_unit) and repairs only by moving the positional unit to first or adding UNIT=; all other specifiers and the open file are unchanged.

requirements.title: ERR labels in CLOSE identify an in-scope branch target statement
requirements.definition: The label used in the ERR= specifier shall be the statement label of a branch target statement in the same inclusive scope as the CLOSE statement.

pending.close-err-label-branch-target: Positive-control source uses ERR=100 with label 100 on a CONTINUE or other branch target in the same scope; a negative repairs an absent/non-branch label only by changing the label target.
pending.close-err-label-same-inclusive-scope: Diagnostic/control source refers to a label outside the inclusive scope, then repairs by adding an equivalent branch target in the CLOSE scope; no runtime error behavior is required.

requirements.title: STATUS character values ignore case and trailing blanks and are limited by the STATUS rule
requirements.definition: The scalar-default-character-expression used for CLOSE STATUS has a limited list of character values; trailing blanks are ignored and matching is case-insensitive.

pending.close-status-values-limited: Use only KEEP and DELETE values enumerated by 12.5.7.3; invalid-value diagnostics are not filed here because p1 is unnumbered and the value list itself is completed in 12.5.7.3.
pending.close-status-trailing-blanks-ignored: Close a named file with STATUS="KEEP   " after writing known content, then reopen and read the content into sentinels; trailing blanks are the only spelling difference from the control.
pending.close-status-case-insensitive: Close separate controlled files with STATUS="keep" and STATUS="DeLeTe" and observe the respective KEEP/DELETE effects fixed by 12.5.7.3; file setup prevents vacuous absence/presence.

review_rationale: Source registration for 12.5.7-12.6.1, the CLOSE statement and data transfer statements in general (batch152). Every unit hash-verified by an independent reviewer across three rounds. Round 1 found a conditional KEEP-on-nonexistent-file plan and scratch DELETE plans that observed only unit closure; both are now explicit no-portable-oracle reasons (no portable way to connect a nonexistent file with KEEP allowed; no portable name for a scratch file), while named-file DELETE keeps a portable EXIST= plan established before the CLOSE. Round 2 found the nonexistent-unit CLOSE plan relied on OPENED=.false.; it is now guarded on INQUIRE EXIST=.false., since no unit number is guaranteed nonexistent. The eight numbered rules were pre-accounted. Source accounting only.
